name: New Zealand Sub-Antarctic Islands
description: Five remote island groups, the Snares, Bounty, Antipodes, Auckland and Campbell, lie scattered across the Southern Ocean southeast of New Zealand. Cold, nutrient-rich seas feed enormous colonies of penguins and seabirds, and 126 bird species have been recorded here, eight of the seabirds breeding nowhere else on Earth. Rare plants and insects thrive on these wind-battered outposts too.
